places.name: Warren Dunes State Park
places.address: 12032 Red Arrow Highway, Sawyer, MI 49125
places.do: Lake Michigan beach under some of the tallest dunes on the shore; swim in the buoyed area, climb Tower Hill, or walk six miles of wooded trails. Paddleboard and kayak rentals in summer.
places.season: Open all year; beach season Memorial Day to Labor Day; cross-country skiing listed as a winter activity. Phone 269-426-4013.
places.fee: Michigan Recreation Passport required for vehicle entry (nonresident day pass $12, annual $42; residents $15 with plate renewal).
places.dogs: Yes, on a 6-foot leash, on the beach north of the northernmost swim buoy (about 2.5 miles of shoreline).
places.access: Three accessible restroom buildings in the beach day-use area; three 100-foot accessible walkways toward the water (they stop short of the water's edge); two beach wheelchairs to borrow at the ranger station.
places.history: Businessman Edward K. Warren bought the dunes and beach as a conservation measure; the land became a state park in 1930.

places.name: Warren Woods State Park
places.address: Warren Woods Road trailhead (Elm Valley Road entrance closed in winter); no street address published
places.do: A quiet one-mile trail along the Galien River through towering beech and sugar maple, with a footbridge over the river; a favorite in spring wildflower season and peak fall color.
places.season: Open all year; the Elm Valley Road entrance is closed in winter, use the Warren Woods Road access. Vault toilet only.
places.dogs: Not stated on the DNR page (state park rule: leashed, 6 feet).
places.history: Edward K. Warren began buying the woods in 1879 to preserve them; the stand, called the last climax beech-maple forest in Michigan, has been a National Natural Landmark since 1967.

places.name: Grand Mere State Park
places.address: No street address published by the DNR (directions link only); off Thornton Drive, Stevensville area — verify
places.do: Hike over wooded dunes to about half a mile of quiet Lake Michigan shoreline, or fish for bluegill on South and Middle lakes; a fine spring birding spot.
places.season: Open all year; snowshoeing in winter. Vault toilets and a picnic pavilion by the main lot.
places.dogs: Yes, on a 6-foot leash, along the half mile of Lake Michigan shoreline.
places.history: Its three inland lakes, remnants of five, formed as the glaciers retreated; the area was named a National Natural Landmark in 1968.

places.name: Van Buren State Park
places.address: 23960 Ruggles Road, South Haven, MI 49090
places.do: A sandy Lake Michigan beach backed by high dunes, with a buoyed swim area, a pet-friendly beach just north of it, and a paved spur to the Van Buren Trail for biking.
places.season: Open all year; paddlesport rentals from the Friday before Memorial Day through Labor Day. Phone 269-637-2788.
places.dogs: Yes, leashed (6 feet), on most of the shoreline except the buoyed swim area; designated pet beach just north of it.
places.access: Track chair to borrow; accessible restroom, parking and a paved walkway to the beach at the swim area; ADA campsites.
places.history: Established in 1966 after the state bought 167 acres from the Harry LaBar Drake family in 1965.

places.name: Silver Beach County Park
places.address: 101 Broad Street, St. Joseph, MI 49085
places.do: A busy, lifeguarded Lake Michigan beach below the bluff with a walk out the South Pier, volleyball courts, playgrounds, and kayak and paddleboard rentals at the north end.
places.season: Open dawn to dusk year-round; restrooms early May to mid-October; lifeguards early June to mid-August. Phone 269-982-0533.
places.fee: Vehicle entry May–September: $8 Berrien County residents, $15 nonresidents; $40 annual Berrien County parks permit. Walk-ins free. Michigan Recreation Passport not accepted.
places.dogs: Leashed on sidewalks only; no pets on the sand or in the water.
places.access: Barrier-free walkway from the lot along the beachfront to the pavilions and South Pier; free beach wheelchair and beach walker in summer, first come first served (ID required, must be pushed).
places.history: Silver Beach became a Berrien County park in the early 1990s.
places.coord_source: US Census Bureau geocoder, from the street address

places.name: Tiscornia Park (Tiscornia Beach)
places.address: 80 Ridgeway Street, St. Joseph, MI 49085
places.do: A 16-acre family beach on the north side of the St. Joseph River mouth with restrooms and a picnic pavilion; walk the North Pier to the two lighthouses at sunset.
places.season: Parking passes required April 1–October 31; lighthouse tours offered between Memorial Day and Labor Day weekends.
places.fee: Paid parking (meter by the hour or day; $40 season city parks pass) April–October. Rates not published on the page we could read.
places.dogs: Leashed dogs on the sidewalk and pier only.
places.history: A light station has stood at the river mouth since 1832; the present North Pier inner and outer lights date from 1906–1907 and are on the National Register of Historic Places.
places.coord_source: Wikipedia coordinates of the North Pier lights (rounded to 0.01°) — approximate

places.name: Jean Klock Park
places.address: Jean Klock Boulevard, Benton Harbor, MI 49022 (no street number published)
places.do: A quieter Lake Michigan beach with a dune observation trail, interdunal wetlands, a marsh and a playground.
places.season: 7 a.m. to 10 p.m. daily (per Visit Southwest Michigan listing). Phone 269-927-8419.
places.fee: Parking kiosks charge May 1–October 30 (minimum three hours, $5, per Visit Southwest Michigan); season passes available — verify current rates with the City of Benton Harbor.
places.history: In 1917 John Nellis Klock and his wife Carrie bought the lakeshore from E. K. Warren and deeded it to the City of Benton Harbor in memory of their daughter Jean.

places.name: Rocky Gap County Park
places.address: 1100 Rocky Gap Road, Benton Harbor, MI 49022
places.do: A small bluff-top park with a Lake Michigan overlook deck and a sandy beach below; a good sunset stop and picnic spot.
places.season: April through October, about 8 a.m. until shortly after sunset; no overnight parking. Vault toilets, no running water.
places.access: Hard-surface ramp to the beach in the lower park.
places.coord_source: US Census Bureau geocoder, from the street address

places.name: Weko Beach
places.address: 5301 Lake Street, Bridgman, MI 49106
places.do: A city beach on Lake Michigan with a boat ramp, campground, and kayak and paddleboard rentals; no lifeguards.
places.season: Park hours 5 a.m. to 11 p.m.; parking fees and rentals Memorial Day to Labor Day. Phone 269-465-3406.
places.fee: $15 per vehicle per day (card only) in season; season passes $10 residents / $45 nonresidents at Bridgman City Hall. Recreation Passport and Berrien County park pass not accepted.
places.dogs: No — dogs prohibited on the beach.

places.name: South Beach (South Haven)
places.address: Beside the south pier at the end of Water Street, South Haven, MI 49090 (no street number published)
places.do: South Haven's signature wide sand beach, a walk from downtown, with the red South Haven lighthouse at the end of the pier; named the 2026 USA TODAY 10Best Readers' Choice best beach in Michigan.
places.season: Summer beach season; city lifeguard program in recent years — verify current dates.
places.fee: Paid parking in season (city rates have been changing; verify with the City of South Haven).
places.dogs: Not stated on the visitor page — check city rules.
places.access: Listed as accessible by Visit South Haven; beach wheelchairs have been donated to South Beach.
places.history: The light station at the mouth of the Black River was lit in 1872; the present tower dates from 1903.
places.coord_source: Wikipedia coordinates of South Haven Light (on the south pier beside the beach) — approximate

places.name: North Beach (South Haven)
places.address: North side of the Black River mouth, South Haven, MI 49090 (no street address published)
places.do: A family beach with a concession stand, picnic area, play equipment, restrooms and volleyball courts, facing the lighthouse across the river.
places.season: Summer season.
places.fee: $10 per trip or $30 weekly parking (per Visit South Haven listing; verify current city rate).

places.name: Dr. T. K. Lawless Park
places.address: 15122 Monkey Run Street, Vandalia, MI 49095
places.do: Cass County's big all-season park: seven miles of hiking trails, ten miles of mountain-bike singletrack, disc golf and a paved one-mile accessible trail by day, and some of the darkest skies in southern Michigan by night, with scheduled public sky-viewing nights.
places.season: Open year-round; hours posted at the park. Winter: seven miles of groomed cross-country ski trail and inner-tube sledding (tubes provided).
places.dogs: Not stated on the county page — check Cass County Parks rules.
places.access: Paved total-access trail (1 mile); modern restrooms; large parking area.
places.history: Accepted as an International Dark Sky Park in January 2020.
places.coord_source: US Census Bureau geocoder, from the street address

places.name: Fred Russ Forest Park
places.address: 20379 Marcellus Highway, Decatur, MI 49045
places.do: A shaded picnic park inside a 580-acre research forest, with four miles of hiking trail, equestrian trails, a canoe landing and trout fishing in a Class A stream.
places.season: Open year-round; four miles of cross-country ski trail in winter. Reservations 269-445-4456 (weekdays 8–4).
places.access: Not stated; rustic restrooms, well water, electricity at shelters.
places.history: The park sits within the 580-acre Fred Russ research forest.

places.name: Arthur Dodd Memorial Park
places.address: 61437 Creek Road, Niles, MI 49120
places.do: A 51-acre park along Dowagiac Creek near the county line with a canoe landing, trout fishing, a one-mile trail and picnic shelters.
places.season: Open year-round, sunrise to sunset.
places.coord_source: US Census Bureau geocoder, from the street address

places.name: Henry Sears Park (Birch Lake access)
places.address: Birch Road and Lake Shore Drive, Cassopolis, MI 49031 (county's listing)
places.do: A small county park on the south side of Birch Lake offering public boat access.
places.season: Not stated.

places.name: Stevens Lakeside Memorial Park
places.address: South off Stevens Forest Lake Road, about 0.2 mile west of Lawrence Road (county's listing gives Cassopolis, MI 49031)
places.do: A two-acre swimming park on the north side of Little Fish Lake with a small picnic shelter and an open games field.
places.season: Not stated.

places.name: Michigan DNR public boating access sites
places.county: Berrien, Cass, Van Buren, St. Joseph, Kalamazoo
places.address: Use the Michigan Boating Facility Finder map for exact locations
places.do: Hundreds of free-to-use state launches; representative Berrien County sites named by the DNR include Paw Paw Lake East and West, Black Lake, the Galien River, Buchanan, New Buffalo, Shamrock Park, Riverview Park and St. Joseph River Park on the St. Joseph River. The finder shows lanes, parking, local watercraft rules and closures.
places.season: Year-round unless posted.
places.fee: Michigan Recreation Passport covers vehicle access to nearly 1,000 state boating access sites.
places.access: Varies by site; see the finder.
places.notes: Site list from the DNR Berrien County facilities sheet: https://www2.dnr.state.mi.us/publications/pdfs/Mi-HUNT/DNRE_Facilities/Berrien.pdf

places.name: St. Patrick's County Park
places.address: 50651 Laurel Road, South Bend, IN 46637
places.do: Riverside park on the St. Joseph River at the state line with hiking trails, a big red barn, a public boat ramp, and canoe and kayak rentals for river trips from Keller Park down to the park or on to the Niles dam.
places.season: Rentals in recent seasons ran late May to early October, Friday–Sunday (verify current schedule). Winter: snowtubing, cross-country ski trails and ski rentals. Phone 574-277-4828.
places.fee: Not stated on the park page — check St. Joseph County Parks.

places.name: Bendix Woods County Park
places.address: 56960 Timothy Road, New Carlisle, IN 46552
places.do: Wooded trails, a 6.5-mile mountain-bike trail, a nature center in the old clubhouse, maple-sugaring in late winter, and the famous pine trees planted to spell STUDEBAKER.
places.season: Open year-round; sledding hill (unsupervised) in winter; Sugar Camp Days in early spring. Phone 574-654-3155.
places.fee: Not stated on the park page — check St. Joseph County Parks.
places.history: Studebaker opened its proving ground here in 1926 and in 1938 planted 8,000 pines that spell STUDEBAKER from the air; the clubhouse and tree sign joined the National Register in 1985.

places.name: Potato Creek State Park
places.address: 25601 State Road 4, North Liberty, IN 46554
places.do: Swim at the Worster Lake beach, rent a canoe, kayak or rowboat (electric motors only), ride the paved bike trail or the 7.4-mile mountain-bike loop, and hike the woods and prairie.
places.season: Daily 7 a.m.–11 p.m. Winter: cross-country skiing (no rentals) and a tubing hill.
places.fee: Indiana state park entrance: $7 per Indiana vehicle, $15 out-of-state; annual pass $50 resident / $120 nonresident.
places.dogs: Not stated on the park page (Indiana state parks generally allow leashed pets outside beaches and buildings — verify).
places.access: Motorized trail wheelchair to borrow; ADA sidewalk from the lot to the water's edge.
places.history: Dedicated as Potato Creek Recreation Area on June 6, 1977, the year its dam created Worster Lake, named for conservationist Darcy Worster; it became a state park in 1983.

places.name: East Race Waterway
places.address: Downtown South Bend along the east bank of the St. Joseph River (no street address on the visitor page)
places.do: A Class II whitewater channel in the heart of downtown where the public can raft (gear provided) or bring their own kayak.
places.season: CLOSED for the 2026 season for updates. Normally June 1–Labor Day, weekends.
places.fee: Normally a $20 day pass with unlimited rides; 54-inch minimum height.
places.history: Dug as an industrial raceway in the late 1800s, later filled in, re-excavated and opened in 1984 as the first man-made whitewater rafting course in North America.

places.name: Fernwood Botanical Garden & Nature Preserve
places.address: 13988 Range Line Road, Niles, MI 49120
places.do: Gardens, an arboretum, tallgrass prairie, a garden railway and woodland trails above the St. Joseph River, with art exhibitions and a café; check in at the Visitors Center first.
places.season: Tuesday–Sunday, 10 a.m.–5 p.m.; closed July 4, Thanksgiving, Dec. 24–25, Dec. 31 and Jan. 1. Some events (such as LIGHTS) cost extra.
places.fee: Adults $12, seniors 65+ $9, youth 5–12 $7, 4 and under free; members free.
places.dogs: No pets (service animals welcome) except at select special events.
places.access: Paved garden paths; group tours can stay on paved paths or move indoors on request.
places.history: Kay and Walter Boydston bought the first 12.5 acres in 1941 as their home; it became a public garden in 1964.

places.name: Sarett Nature Center
places.address: 2300 N. Benton Center Road, Benton Harbor, MI 49022
places.do: Nine miles of trails through river bottomland, woods and wetland, boardwalks, a treetop walkway, a nature play area and a summer Butterfly House; a fine place to bird.
places.season: Trails dawn to dusk daily; building Tuesday–Saturday 10–5, Sunday 1–5, closed Monday; Butterfly House May–September. Winter: cross-country ski and snowshoe rentals. Phone 269-927-4832.
places.fee: Nonmember adults $3; children and members free. Butterfly House extra ($8 adults, $5 children, nonmembers).
places.dogs: No — pets not allowed on trails or in buildings.
places.access: An accessible trail; trail accessibility vehicles available (see sarett.org/trailaccessibility).
places.history: Founded in 1963 when Elizabeth and William Vawter bought 130 acres and Michigan Audubon agreed to manage it; named for the naturalist and poet Lew Sarett.
places.coord_source: US Census Bureau geocoder, from the street address

places.name: Dowagiac Woods Nature Sanctuary
places.address: Frost Road, one mile east of Sink Road (from Dowagiac take M-62 west to Sink Road, south 1 mile to Frost Road, east 1 mile); no street number published
places.do: Walk a 1.5-mile trail through a never-plowed woodland famous for spring wildflowers, especially more than 150 beds of blue-eyed Mary; over 400 plant species grow here.
places.season: Open year-round; best late April to mid-May for wildflowers. Trail can be wet in spring.
places.dogs: Not stated — check the Michigan Nature Association's sanctuary visitation rules before bringing a dog.
places.history: Established by the Michigan Nature Association in 1981 and enlarged to 384 acres in 2009.

places.name: Love Creek County Park & Nature Center
places.address: 9292 Huckleberry Road, Berrien Center, MI 49102
places.do: Nine miles of trails through 200 rolling acres along Love Creek, including mature beech-maple woods with spring wildflowers, plus a 3.5-mile mountain-bike loop and a nature center.
places.season: Open year-round, daylight hours; nature center Wednesday–Sunday 10–5. Winter: groomed classic and skate ski trails with rentals, and groomed fat-bike trail with rentals. Phone 269-471-2617.
places.fee: $3 per vehicle Berrien County residents, $5 nonresidents; annual permits available.
places.dogs: Leashed dogs on trails when there is no snow; no dogs once trails are groomed for skiing.
places.coord_source: US Census Bureau geocoder, from the street address

places.name: Kalamazoo Nature Center
places.address: 7000 North Westnedge Avenue, Kalamazoo, MI 49009
places.do: About 14 miles of trails across more than a thousand acres of woods, prairie and wetland north of the city, with a visitor center and accessible arboretum trails.
places.season: Visitor Center Mon–Sat 9–5, Sun 1–5; trails 9 a.m.–7:30 p.m. March–October, 9–5 November–February. Phone 269-381-1574.
places.fee: Adults $8, 55+ and military $6, children 4–17 $6, 3 and under free.
places.dogs: No — pets not permitted anywhere on the property, even leashed.
places.access: GRIT Freedom all-terrain wheelchairs to reserve; Habitat Haven and Arboretum trails wheelchair- and stroller-accessible; accessible visitor center.
places.history: Founded October 31, 1960, by Kalamazoo community leaders who pooled resources to buy land for an outdoor education center.
places.coord_source: US Census Bureau geocoder, from the street address

places.name: Bonneyville Mill County Park
places.address: 53373 County Road 131, Bristol, IN 46507
places.do: See the state's oldest operating grist mill grinding grain, then walk seven miles of trails along the Little Elkhart River, fish for bass and stocked trout, or ride the mountain-bike trail.
places.season: Park open daily (9 a.m. to 6–9 p.m. by month); mill Tuesday–Sunday 10–5 in season (closes in early-to-mid November — confirm). Winter: cross-country skiing and two sledding hills.
places.history: Built by Edward Bonney in 1832; listed on the National Register of Historic Places in 1976.

places.name: Kal-Haven Trail State Park
places.address: Trailheads in South Haven and Kalamazoo, with access at Grand Junction, Bloomingdale and Alamo (no street addresses on the DNR page)
places.do: Ride or walk about 34 miles of crushed limestone between Lake Michigan and Kalamazoo through farms, woods and small trail towns; a hybrid or gravel bike suits it better than a road bike.
places.season: Year-round; cross-country skiing allowed (not groomed); snowmobiles Dec. 1–March 31. Phone 269-637-2788.
places.fee: No trail-use fee stated (the county trail pass was dropped in 2011); Recreation Passport for state park vehicle entry where applicable.
places.dogs: Not stated on the DNR page (state rule: leashed, 6 feet).
places.history: Built on the bed of the Kalamazoo and South Haven Railroad (1870s), abandoned in 1973; the trail opened August 15, 1989.

places.name: Van Buren Trail State Park
places.address: South Haven to Hartford; spur from Van Buren State Park (no street address on the DNR page)
places.do: A 14-mile former rail line: two paved miles from South Haven to 16th Avenue, then gravel to Hartford suited to mountain bikes and horses; links to the Kal-Haven Trail.
places.season: Year-round; skiing allowed (not groomed); snowmobiles on 13 miles Dec. 1–March 31.
places.history: Follows a former railroad right-of-way.

places.name: Indiana-Michigan River Valley Trail
places.address: Endpoints: Plym Park, 401 Marmont Street, Niles, MI, and Logan Street, Mishawaka, IN
places.do: A paved riverside route linking Niles, South Bend and Mishawaka past more than 15 parks, Notre Dame and four downtowns; join it anywhere for a walk or a long ride across the state line.
places.season: Year-round.
places.coord_source: US Census Bureau geocoder, from the street address
places.notes: Length listed inconsistently on TrailLink (32.7 miles in the header, 17 paved miles in the text).

places.name: Mishawaka Riverwalk
places.address: Loop along both banks of the St. Joseph River; east end at Logan Street near Central Park (295 E. Mishawaka Avenue)
places.do: A 2.6-mile paved loop on both banks of the river, crossing a suspension bridge and a boardwalk near the dam and fish ladder, past Battell Park, Central Park, Beutter Riverfront Park and Kamm Island.
places.season: Year-round.
places.access: Asphalt, brick and concrete; the Battell Park section is wide paved concrete suitable for strollers and mobility devices.
places.coord_source: US Census Bureau geocoder, from the street address

places.name: Riverfront Park (Niles)
places.address: Water Street, Niles, MI 49120 (no street number published)
places.do: The city's park on the St. Joseph River with walking paths, fishing and boating, a playground, skate park and amphitheater that hosts summer concerts; the river trail to South Bend starts nearby at Plym Park.
places.season: Year-round. Phone 269-683-4700.

places.name: Pumpkinvine Nature Trail
places.address: Trail access in Goshen, Middlebury and Shipshewana (see pumpkinvine.org Trail Information)
places.do: A completed 17-mile paved greenway through Amish farm country linking Goshen, Middlebury and Shipshewana — slow down for buggies and bicycles alike.
places.season: Year-round.
places.history: Built on the old Pumpkinvine railroad corridor; the Friends of the Pumpkinvine began the conversion in 1992 and the full 17 miles were completed in June 2024.
places.notes: Shipshewana lies in LaGrange County, Indiana (not LaGrange Township, Cass County).

places.name: MapleHeart Trail
places.address: Between E. Hively Avenue (Elkhart) and Lincolnway North (Goshen)
places.do: A nearly five-mile paved rail-trail from Elkhart south to the edge of Goshen, linking the River Greenway with the Pumpkinvine network.
places.season: Year-round.
places.notes: Verified only on TrailLink; no official managing site found.

places.name: River Greenway Trail (Elkhart)
places.address: Trailhead at the Elkhart Environmental Center, 1717 E. Lusher Avenue, Elkhart, IN 46516
places.do: Follow the Elkhart River from the Environmental Center into the downtown River District, with a connection to the MapleHeart Trail toward Goshen.
places.season: Year-round.
places.coord_source: US Census Bureau geocoder, from the street address

places.name: St. Joseph River Water Trail (Michigan)
places.address: Access sites in Niles, Buchanan, Berrien Springs, Benton Harbor and St. Joseph (interactive map on the trail page)
places.do: About 67 river miles from Niles to Lake Michigan with good fishing; plan portages at the dams in Niles, Buchanan and Berrien Springs, and watch for big boats and freighters in the working harbor at the mouth.
places.season: Spring through fall; check flows and weather.
places.fee: Free (Recreation Passport for vehicles at state launches).
places.notes: Managed in information by the Southwest Michigan Planning Commission (swmpc.org/swmi_watertrails.asp).

places.name: Dowagiac River Water Trail
places.address: Access points on the trail-page map; last access before the St. Joseph is the DNR site on M-139 just north of Niles
places.do: Southern Michigan's largest coldwater river, moderately fast through trees and wetlands. The stretch below Dodd Park to the former Pucker Street Dam site has significant logjams and is for advanced paddlers only.
places.season: Spring through fall; stay off after heavy rain. USGS gage: waterdata.usgs.gov site 04101800.
places.history: The Pucker Street dam has been removed.
places.notes: A canoe and kayak livery on M-51 north of Dowagiac (paddledcri.com) offers 2–6 hour trips; its site blocked our reader, so details are unverified.

places.name: Paw Paw River Water Trail
places.address: Begins below the Maple Lake Dam in the Village of Paw Paw; access map on the trail page
places.do: A 68-mile winding river trail past Lawrence, Hartford, Watervliet, Coloma and Riverside to its meeting with the St. Joseph near Lake Michigan; expect fallen trees.
places.season: Spring through fall; check the USGS gage (04102500) before going.

places.name: Galien River Marsh Water Trail
places.address: See trail page
places.do: A marsh paddle near the Lake Michigan shore, listed by the Southwest Michigan Planning Commission among the region's water trails.
places.season: Spring through fall.

places.name: Elkhart River canoe trips (Goshen Parks)
places.address: Reserve at the Goshen Parks office, 410 W. Plymouth Avenue, Goshen, IN; launch at Shanklin Park, take-out at Ox Bow
places.do: A roughly four-hour canoe trip down the Elkhart River from Shanklin Park to Ox Bow; the city drops the canoe at the launch (no shuttle back from Ox Bow — arrange your own return).
places.season: April 15–October 15; reserve 96 hours ahead at 574-534-2901.
places.fee: $40 plus tax per canoe (two adults and two children, or three adults).
places.coord_source: US Census Bureau geocoder, from the street address

places.name: Fidler Pond Park boat rentals
places.address: Fidler Pond Park, 1424 Lincolnway East, Goshen, IN
places.do: Rent a canoe, kayak or paddleboard by the hour on a calm city pond — a good first paddle for children.
places.season: Weekends late May through August (check dates), from 10 a.m. until an hour before dusk.
places.fee: $10 per boat per hour; life jackets mandatory.
places.coord_source: US Census Bureau geocoder, from the street address

places.name: Liquid Therapy Canoe & Kayak Rental
places.address: 221 S. Main Street, Three Rivers, MI 49093
places.do: Canoe and kayak trips on the St. Joseph, Rocky, Portage and Prairie rivers around Three Rivers.
places.season: Launches seven days a week Memorial Day–Labor Day. Phone 269-273-9000.
places.coord_source: US Census Bureau geocoder, from the street address
places.notes: Listing from Pure Michigan; no business website found.

places.name: Beardsley Park kayak launch (Elkhart)
places.address: 135 E. Beardsley Avenue, Elkhart, IN
places.do: An ADA-compliant kayak launch and fishing access on the north bank of the St. Joseph River just east of Main Street.
places.season: Year-round.
places.coord_source: US Census Bureau geocoder, from the street address

upick.name: Stover's Farm Market & U-Pic
upick.fruit: Strawberries, sweet and tart cherries, red and black raspberries, peaches (nine varieties), apples (23 varieties), pumpkins, gourds, squash
upick.months: Late May/early June (strawberries) through October (pumpkins and squash); call ahead, dates follow the weather
upick.notes: Farm's own site blocked our reader; details from Visit Southwest Michigan.
upick.coord_source: US Census Bureau geocoder, from the street address

upick.name: Fruit Acres Farm Market & U-Pick
upick.address: U-pick: 2789 Friday Road, Coloma, MI 49038 (market: 3452 Friday Road)
upick.fruit: Sweet and tart cherries, peaches, apples, pumpkins
upick.months: Peaches mid-July through September; apples late summer–fall; u-pick Saturdays and Sundays 10–4:30
upick.notes: Some availability notes on the site are old; check before going.
upick.coord_source: US Census Bureau geocoder, from the street address

upick.name: Jollay Orchards
upick.fruit: Cherries, blueberries and peaches in summer; apples and grapes in fall
upick.notes: Admission and hours on the farm's Summer Hours page.
upick.coord_source: US Census Bureau geocoder, from the street address

upick.name: Lehman's Orchard
upick.fruit: Raspberries, blackberries, tomatoes, apples (Honeycrisp and more); also listed for blueberries, cherries and currants
upick.months: Summer into fall (2026 season listed raspberries and blackberries, with more apples from August)
upick.notes: No animals in the fields (food-safety rule). Phone 269-683-9078.
upick.coord_source: US Census Bureau geocoder, from the street address

upick.address: 76241 14th Avenue, South Haven, MI 49090 (address from PickYourOwn.org; not shown on the visitor page)
upick.months: Blueberries July–August; cranberry season October–November with harvest festival days the first two Saturdays of October
upick.notes: Farm's own site blocked our reader.

upick.address: 5118 Hollywood Road, St. Joseph, MI 49085 (from PickYourOwn.org)
upick.notes: UNVERIFIED on the farm's own site (robots blocked); confirm before listing.
upick.coord_source: US Census Bureau geocoder, from the street address

upick.name: Nye's Apple Barn
upick.address: 3151 Niles Avenue (M-63), St. Joseph, MI 49085 (from PickYourOwn.org)
upick.fruit: Apples, grapes, peaches, cherries, blackberries, raspberries

getting_here.drive_note: Free-flow routing estimates from the OSRM public router (router.project-osrm.org) between city-center coordinates from Wikipedia and Cassopolis (41.91083, -86.00778); allow extra time for traffic, especially around Chicago.
getting_here.time_zones: All of southwest Michigan (Berrien, Cass, Van Buren, St. Joseph, Kalamazoo) and Indiana's St. Joseph and Elkhart counties keep Eastern time. LaPorte County, Indiana (Michigan City and La Porte), keeps Central time, as does Chicago — so the clock jumps an hour when you cross into LaPorte County or ride the South Shore Line west of it.
getting_here.ev_charging: For public chargers along I-94, US-12, US-31 and M-62, use the U.S. Department of Energy's station locator: https://afdc.energy.gov/stations

meta.recreation_passport: Michigan Recreation Passport: $15 resident annual with plate renewal (2-year $29); nonresident $12 daily, $42 annual; covers vehicle entry to all 103 state parks and recreation areas and nearly 1,000 boating access sites. Source: https://www.michigan.gov/dnr/buy-and-apply/recreation-passport
meta.indiana_state_parks: Indiana state parks: $7 per Indiana vehicle, $15 out-of-state per day at most parks; annual $50 resident, $120 nonresident. Source: https://secure.in.gov/dnr/state-parks/rates-and-fees/entrance-fees
meta.excluded: Harmon Park (Cass County Parks) was left out because it is on Shavehead Lake. Nothing in LaGrange Township (Cass Co.), Kelsey Lake, Stone Lake or Ramptown is listed. No tribal places, businesses or staff are listed.
meta.not_found: No Iron Belle Trail segment was found in these counties on the DNR page (its hiking route runs through Albion/Jackson and its bike route on the east side) — verify on the DNR interactive map before mentioning it. East Race Waterway is closed for 2026.
